stage: Primary same-later-cohort comparison and atomic model/threshold lifecycle
findings: The trainer promoted its candidate before the retrain wrapper compared reported scores from different populations
Post-hoc rollback restored model/meta/global threshold aliases, but not the registry and per-lane thresholds
Model/meta/threshold aliases were replaced separately, allowing a partially updated reader snapshot
A newest-by-timestamp candidate could become the primary inference fallback without explicit activation
Primary registry rewrites could discard independently maintained family headers; corrupt registry reads could silently reset state
A worker diagnostic gate snapshot could overwrite the current model/threshold view, and per-lane modes were not distinguished from uniform primary enforcement

implementation.reservation: Reserve a later settled token-disjoint net-outcome cohort before feature/model/threshold selection. Final fitting/calibration never uses the reserved cohort. Earlier fit labels must mature before the next decision with a 60-second embargo
implementation.freshness: Exclude all previous incumbent fit and approval tokens and require decisions after both previous label-availability boundaries. Replaying the same cohort cannot create fresh approval
implementation.comparison: Evaluate frozen candidate and incumbent probability models/thresholds on exactly the same later checked net population with the same positive-label target. Ignore old reported AUC/EV scores. Without a checked incumbent, compare with an explicitly zero-admission label-proxy baseline; archive legacy bytes without pretending they are a comparable champion
implementation.support: At least 30 independent tokens, five positive and five negative tokens, configured selected-row/precision support and five selected tokens. Require positive selected average net labels, probability loss skill against older fit prevalence and positive paired token-cluster lower net-label-proxy improvement above configured ML_SELECTION_MIN_DELTA
implementation.atomic_bundle: Write immutable fsync-backed model, metadata, global threshold, per-lane thresholds and exact checksummed approval. One atomic registry replacement selects the complete bundle. An OS-owned nonblocking writer lock plus expected-incumbent compare-and-swap prevents stale/concurrent overwrite
implementation.readers: Primary inference resolves the checked selector bundle, verifies all component hashes, schema, chronological probability/model/calibrator binding and approval, then pins it per entry decision. Corrupt selection/components are unknown; good stale mirrors and newer unapproved candidates cannot resurrect inference
implementation.rollback: Validate the checked previous bundle before atomically swapping complete references. Keep family/custom registry headers. A corrupt previous bundle cannot replace a healthy active one. Compatibility aliases are post-commit mirrors, not authority
implementation.acknowledgement: Mirror or train-status export failures after selector commit are publication warnings, not an instruction to restore old aliases. TrainResult returns actual immutable selected paths and promotion outcome; retrain no longer backs up/restores files or compares unrelated run scores
implementation.diagnostics: API current model/threshold view cannot be overwritten by an older worker gate snapshot. Per-lane and sizing/risk-only modes are not presented as a uniform primary probability gate
implementation.migration: Legacy artifacts remain untouched in this stage. First future gated promotion archives legacy model/meta/threshold bytes. Legacy artifacts without primary probability evidence remain unknown; candidate fallback configuration is deprecated and ignored
implementation.upside_and_size: Exact requested 0.1 SOL paper orders and uncapped runner upside are unchanged. Existing synthetic exit tests exercise 500, 1000, 5000, 10000 and 100000 percent peaks, distinguish peak-price drawdown from profit points and retain liquidity/holding safeguards
